The text discusses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its subfield, machine learning, highlighting applications such as voice recognition (e.g., Siri) and autonomous vehicles. In the context of database systems, these concepts relate to several key areas. Machine learning algorithms often rely on large-scale data storage solutions, such as NoSQL databases or data lakes, to store the training data required for models to improve through experience. Voice recognition systems like Siri utilize Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, which depend on extensive linguistic databases and vector databases for efficient semantic search and retrieval. Furthermore, autonomous vehicles generate and process massive amounts of real-time sensor data, requiring high-throughput, low-latency database architectures to manage navigation maps, traffic patterns, and vehicle telemetry. These database technologies enable the scalability and speed necessary for AI systems to interact effectively with humans and their environments.
